interventions.name: Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP)
synonyms: adapted lifestyle behavior change programs for diabetes prevention
interventions.source_text: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) “Standards of Care in Diabetes” includes the ADA’s current clinical practice recommendations and is intended to provide the components of diabetes care, general treatment goals and guidelines, and tools to evaluate quality of care.
interventions.duration: 16-session structured core curriculum, completed within the first 6 months of the program, followed by an additional 6 months of a flexible maintenance program

interventions.name: Metformin
interventions.source_text: Metformin has the most robust efficacy and safety data as a pharmacologic therapy for diabetes prevention among people with prediabetes (82).

interventions.name: Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT)
interventions.source_text: For people at risk for or living with diabetes, individualized medical nutrition therapy (see section 5, “Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes,” for more detailed information) is effective in lowering A1C (29,30).

interventions.name: Technology-assisted diabetes prevention programs
interventions.source_text: Based on individual preference, certified technology-assisted diabetes prevention programs through smartphones, web-based applications, and telehealth can be effective in preventing type 2 diabetes and should be considered. B

interventions.name: Teplizumab-mzwv infusion
interventions.source_text: Teplizumab-mzwv infusion to delay the onset of symptomatic type 1 diabetes (stage 3) should be discussed with selected individuals aged ≥8 years with stage 2 type 1 diabetes. Treatment should be in a setting with appropriately trained personnel.

interventions.name: Lifestyle intervention
interventions.source_text: Several major randomized controlled trials, including the Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) (8), the Finnish Diabetes Prevention Study (DPS) (9), and the Da Qing Diabetes Prevention Study (Da Qing study) (10), demonstrated that lifestyle/behavioral intervention with an individualized reduced-calorie meal plan is highly effective in preventing or delaying type 2 diabetes and improving other cardiometabolic risk factors such as blood pressure, lipids, and markers of inflammation (11).

interventions.name: Metformin for prevention of type 2 diabetes
interventions.source_text: Metformin for the prevention of type 2 diabetes should be considered in adults at high risk of type 2 diabetes, as typified by the Diabetes Prevention Program, especially those aged 25–59 years with BMI ≥35 kg/m², higher fasting plasma glucose (e.g., ≥110 mg/dL [≥6 mmol/L]), and higher A1C (e.g., ≥6.0% [≥42 mmol/mol]).

interventions.name: Metformin to prevent hyperglycemia in high-risk individuals treated with a phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase α (PI3Kα) inhibitor
interventions.source_text: Consider using metformin to prevent hyperglycemia in high-risk individuals treated with a phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase α (PI3Kα) inhibitor (e.g., alpelisib and inavolisib). B

interventions.name: Metformin to prevent hyperglycemia in high-risk individuals treated with high-dose glucocorticoids
interventions.source_text: Consider using metformin to prevent hyperglycemia in high-risk individuals treated with high-dose glucocorticoids. B

interventions.name: Diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES)
interventions.source_text: Diabetes self-management education and support in adults with type 2 diabetes: a consensus report of the American Diabetes Association, the Association of Diabetes Care & Education Specialists, the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, the American Academy of Family Physicians, the American Academy of PAs, the American Association of Nurse Practitioners, and the American Pharmacists Association. Diabetes Care 2022;45:2753–2786

interventions.name: Testosterone therapy
interventions.source_text: Testosterone therapy also reduced the risk of incident type 2 diabetes by 41% in men aged 50–74 years with central obesity and prediabetes (89). However, the benefit of testosterone was observed only when added to a structured lifestyle program.

interventions.name: Vitamin D therapy
interventions.source_text: There has been significant interest in understanding the potential of vitamin D therapy to prevent progression of high-risk prediabetes to type 2 diabetes in adults (91).

interventions.name: Glucagon-like peptide 1–based therapies for weight management
interventions.source_text: use of glucagon-like peptide 1–based therapies for weight management in individuals with overweight or obesity—an essential component of type 2 diabetes prevention—is highly beneficial and should be considered, as discussed in detail in section 8, “Obesity and Weight Management for the Prevention and Treatment of Diabetes.”

interventions.name: Pioglitazone
interventions.source_text: The IRIS (Insulin Resistance Intervention after Stroke) trial of people with a recent (<6 months) stroke or transient ischemic attack, without diabetes but with insulin resistance (as defined by a HOMA of insulin resistance index of ≥3.0), evaluated pioglitazone (goal dose of 45 mg daily) compared with placebo.

behaviors.name: Monitor for development of diabetes
synonyms: monitor for the development of diabetes
behaviors.source_text: In people with prediabetes, monitor for the development of diabetes at least annually; modify frequency of testing based on individual risk assessment. E

behaviors.name: Modify frequency of testing based on individual risk assessment
behaviors.source_text: In people with prediabetes, monitor for the development of diabetes at least annually; modify frequency of testing based on individual risk assessment. E

behaviors.name: Assess risk factors for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes
behaviors.source_text: Screening for prediabetes (which refers to hyperglycemia preceding the diagnosis of type 2 diabetes only) and type 2 diabetes risk through an assessment of risk factors (Table 2.5) or with an assessment tool, such as the American Diabetes Association risk test, which can be used by either a layperson or a health care professional (diabetes.org/diabetes-risk-test), is recommended to guide whether to perform a diagnostic test for prediabetes (Table 2.2) and type 2 diabetes (Table 2.1) (see section 2, “Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes”).

behaviors.name: Mediterranean eating pattern
behaviors.source_text: Prescribe an evidence-based eating pattern (e.g., Mediterranean, low carbohydrate) to individuals with prediabetes to prevent type 2 diabetes. B

behaviors.name: Low carbohydrate eating pattern
behaviors.source_text: Prescribe an evidence-based eating pattern (e.g., Mediterranean, low carbohydrate) to individuals with prediabetes to prevent type 2 diabetes. B

behaviors.name: Participate in diabetes prevention programs
behaviors.source_text: Offer diabetes prevention programs to adults at high risk for type 2 diabetes. A

behaviors.name: Achieve and maintain at least 7% weight loss
behaviors.source_text: Two major goals of the DPP were to achieve and maintain at least 7% weight loss and to obtain 150 min of moderate-intensity physical activity per week, such as brisk walking.

behaviors.name: Obtain 150 min of moderate-intensity physical activity per week
synonyms: 150 min of moderate-intensity physical activity per week
behaviors.source_text: Two major goals of the DPP were to achieve and maintain at least 7% weight loss and to obtain 150 min of moderate-intensity physical activity per week, such as brisk walking.

behaviors.name: Distribute physical activity throughout the week
behaviors.source_text: Participants were encouraged to distribute physical activity throughout the week with a minimum frequency of three times per week and at least 10 min per session.
behaviors.target_amount: minimum frequency of three times per week and at least 10 min per session

behaviors.name: Reduce total fat intake
behaviors.source_text: The initial focus of the nutrition intervention was on reducing total fat intake rather than caloric restriction. However, the concepts of calorie balance and the need to restrict total calories and fat were also introduced.

behaviors.name: Reduce total calories
behaviors.source_text: However, the concepts of calorie balance and the need to restrict total calories and fat were also introduced.

behaviors.name: Lose 1–2 lb/week
behaviors.source_text: The recommended pace of weight loss was 1–2 lb/week.

behaviors.name: Consume whole grains
behaviors.source_text: The overall quality of food consumed (as measured by the Healthy Eating Index, Alternative Healthy Eating Index, and DASH score), with an emphasis on whole grains, legumes, nuts, fruits, and vegetables and minimal refined and processed foods, is also associated with a lower risk of type 2 diabetes (26–28).

behaviors.name: Engage in resistance training
behaviors.source_text: In addition to aerobic activity, a physical activity plan designed to prevent diabetes can include resistance training (17,33).

behaviors.name: Break up prolonged sedentary time
behaviors.source_text: Breaking up prolonged sedentary time may also be encouraged, as it lowers postprandial glucose levels (34).

behaviors.name: Increase physical activity
behaviors.source_text: Individuals with prediabetes can benefit from counseling by a registered dietitian nutritionist, which has been shown to help improve eating habits, increase physical activity, and achieve 7–10% weight loss (50–53).

behaviors.name: Improve eating habits
behaviors.source_text: Individuals with prediabetes can benefit from counseling by a registered dietitian nutritionist, which has been shown to help improve eating habits, increase physical activity, and achieve 7–10% weight loss (50–53).

behaviors.name: Achieve 7–10% weight loss
behaviors.source_text: Individuals with prediabetes can benefit from counseling by a registered dietitian nutritionist, which has been shown to help improve eating habits, increase physical activity, and achieve 7–10% weight loss (50–53).

behaviors.name: Adhere to DPP content
behaviors.source_text: Interventions to prevent type 2 diabetes can also be delivered through workplace programming, with interventions that most closely adhere to DPP content shown to be most effective (45).

behaviors.name: Participate in DPP-based interventions
behaviors.source_text: The CDC Diabetes Prevention Recognition Program (DPRP) (https://www.cdc.gov/diabetes-prevention/php/program-provider/program-requirements.html) certifies technology-assisted modalities as effective vehicles for DPP-based interventions; such programs must use an approved curriculum, include interaction with a coach, and attain the DPP outcomes of participation, physical activity reporting, and weight loss.

behaviors.name: Report physical activity
behaviors.source_text: The CDC Diabetes Prevention Recognition Program (DPRP) (https://www.cdc.gov/diabetes-prevention/php/program-provider/program-requirements.html) certifies technology-assisted modalities as effective vehicles for DPP-based interventions; such programs must use an approved curriculum, include interaction with a coach, and attain the DPP outcomes of participation, physical activity reporting, and weight loss.

behaviors.source_text: The CDC Diabetes Prevention Recognition Program (DPRP) (https://www.cdc.gov/diabetes-prevention/php/program-provider/program-requirements.html) certifies technology-assisted modalities as effective vehicles for DPP-based interventions; such programs must use an approved curriculum, include interaction with a coach, and attain the DPP outcomes of participation, physical activity reporting, and weight loss.

behaviors.name: Increase physical activity
behaviors.source_text: The CDC’s Division of Diabetes Translation National DPP toolkit (coveragetoolkit.org/recruitment-referral-for-the-national-dpp-lifestyle-change-program) provides diabetes care team members resources for how to increase referral and uptake of the DPP.

behaviors.name: Consume an individualized reduced-calorie meal plan
behaviors.source_text: Several major randomized controlled trials, including the Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) (8), the Finnish Diabetes Prevention Study (DPS) (9), and the Da Qing Diabetes Prevention Study (Da Qing study) (10), demonstrated that lifestyle/behavioral intervention with an individualized reduced-calorie meal plan is highly effective in preventing or delaying type 2 diabetes and improving other cardiometabolic risk factors such as blood pressure, lipids, and markers of inflammation (11).

behaviors.name: Monitor vitamin B12 levels
synonyms: periodic assessment of vitamin B12 levels
behaviors.source_text: Consider periodic assessment of vitamin B12 levels in individuals receiving long-term metformin therapy, especially in those with anemia or peripheral neuropathy. B

behaviors.name: Consume a plant-based eating pattern
behaviors.source_text: A variety of eating patterns (21) can be appropriate for individuals with prediabetes or diabetes, including Mediterranean-style, plant-based (which may or may not be omnivorous), Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), and low-carbohydrate (22–25).

behaviors.name: Consume a DASH eating pattern
behaviors.source_text: A variety of eating patterns (21) can be appropriate for individuals with prediabetes or diabetes, including Mediterranean-style, plant-based (which may or may not be omnivorous), Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), and low-carbohydrate (22–25).

behaviors.name: Monitor for adverse events of metformin therapy
behaviors.source_text: However, it is important to weigh the benefits of preventing hyperglycemia with the potential adverse effects of metformin therapy, particularly diarrhea, which is also a frequent adverse effect of PI3Kα therapy (though there is no evidence that concurrent use of these two medications further exacerbates diarrhea risk) (108).

behaviors.name: Consume less than 6 hours of sleep
behaviors.source_text: There is now established evidence for a U-shaped association between sleep duration and type 2 diabetes incidence, with the nadir typically occurring at 7 h per day, with short (typically defined as <6 h) and long (typically defined as >9 h) sleep duration having up to a 50% increase in the risk of type 2 diabetes, including progression from prediabetes (70).

behaviors.name: Consume more than 9 hours of sleep
behaviors.source_text: There is now established evidence for a U-shaped association between sleep duration and type 2 diabetes incidence, with the nadir typically occurring at 7 h per day, with short (typically defined as <6 h) and long (typically defined as >9 h) sleep duration having up to a 50% increase in the risk of type 2 diabetes, including progression from prediabetes (70).

behaviors.name: Improve sleep quality
behaviors.source_text: Sleep quality is defined as “an individual’s self-satisfaction with all aspects of the sleep experience” (71,72). A meta-analysis reported that poor overall sleep quality was associated with a 40% increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes (73).

behaviors.name: Adopt a morning chronotype
behaviors.source_text: Chronotype preference has been linked with many chronic diseases, including type 2 diabetes. For example, for those with a preference for evenings (i.e., going to bed late and getting up late), there was a 2.5-fold higher odds ratio for type 2 diabetes than for those with a preference for mornings (i.e., going to bed early and getting up early), independent of sleep duration and sleep sufficiency (74).

behaviors.name: Avoid evening chronotype
behaviors.source_text: Chronotype preference has been linked with many chronic diseases, including type 2 diabetes. For example, for those with a preference for evenings (i.e., going to bed late and getting up late), there was a 2.5-fold higher odds ratio for type 2 diabetes than for those with a preference for mornings (i.e., going to bed early and getting up early), independent of sleep duration and sleep sufficiency (74).

behaviors.name: Engage in lifestyle interventions
behaviors.source_text: Testosterone therapy also reduced the risk of incident type 2 diabetes by 41% in men aged 50–74 years with central obesity and prediabetes (89). However, the benefit of testosterone was observed only when added to a structured lifestyle program.

behaviors.name: Lose weight
behaviors.source_text: The IRIS (Insulin Resistance Intervention after Stroke) trial of people with a recent (<6 months) stroke or transient ischemic attack, without diabetes but with insulin resistance (as defined by a HOMA of insulin resistance index of ≥3.0), evaluated pioglitazone (goal dose of 45 mg daily) compared with placebo. At 4.8 years, the risk of stroke or myocardial infarction, as well as the risk of diabetes, was lower in the pioglitazone group than in the placebo group; weight gain, edema, and fractures were higher in the pioglitazone treatment group (128–130).

behaviors.name: Minimize progression of hyperglycemia
behaviors.source_text: In adults with overweight or obesity at high risk of type 2 diabetes, care goals should include weight Loss and maintenance, minimizing the progression of hyperglycemia, and attention to cardiovascular risk.
